chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Amr Al-Kinani, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Amr! What is your view if I were to narrate to you a hadith or issue a verdict to you, then you come to me after that and ask me about it, so I inform you with a statement contrary to what I had informed you, or issue a verdict contrary to that, which of the two would you take?' I said, 'I take the newer of the two and leave the other one.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You are correct, O Abu Amr! Allah refused except that He be worshipped in secret. But, by Allah, if you were to do that, it would be better for me and for you; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refused for us and for you in His religion, except for dissimulation (taqiyya).'

key_terms.أَحْدَثِهِمَا: The newer of the two; referring to the most recent statement or ruling.
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation; the practice of concealing one's true beliefs or rulings to avoid harm or for divine wisdom.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific title for Allah.

ai.seo_question: What is the theological basis for Taqiyya in Shia Islam according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal principle of 'naskh al-ifta' (abrogation of fatwas), where the most recent statement of the Imam prevails over previous ones, reflecting the dynamic nature of religious guidance. The Imam links this practical mechanism to the divine decree of 'Taqiyya' (dissimulation), asserting that concealing the truth when necessary is not merely a political strategy but a fundamental religious obligation ('ibadah') ordained by Allah for the preservation of the faith.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Amro Al Kinany who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Amro! What is your view if I<sup>asws</sup> were to narrate to you a Hadeeth or issue a Verdict to you, then you come over to me after that and ask me about it, so I<sup>asws</sup> inform you with different to what I<sup>asws</sup> had informed you beforehand, or issue a verdict different (statement) to that, which of the two would you be taking with?’ I said, ‘With the latest of the two and leave the other one’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said:’ You are correct, O Abu Amro! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Refused except that He<sup>azwj</sup> be worshipped in secret. But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, if you all were to do that it would be better for me<sup>asws</sup> and for you all; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Refused for us<sup>asws</sup> and you all with regards to His<sup>azwj</sup> Religion, except for the dissimulation’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Amr al-Kinani who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘O abu ‘Amr, what would you do, were I to narrate a Hadith to you or give you a Fatwa (a legal opinion), and you came to me sometimes later to ask about the same issues, but I gave you a Hadith or a Fatwa that contradicts the first one, which one would you follow?’ I said, ‘I will follow the latest one and ignore the other one.’

The Imam said, ‘O abu ‘Amr, you are right. Allah refuses to accept anything but to worship Him secretly. By Allah, were you to follow al-Taqiyyah it would be better for you and for me. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, refuses to accept anything from you and I in His religion but al-Taqiyyah.’”
